description.p: Xtrude CAD is a 3D modeller for precise technical parts that will be 3D-printed: robot parts, brackets, enclosures, PCB mounts, servo horns. You draw a profile on a face and push or pull it into a solid, typing exact lengths as you go.

Documents are in millimetres by default. Lines, rectangles, circles and arcs snap to edges, midpoints and axes; offset, fillet, sweep, move, rotate and scale shape the model; groups and components keep repeated parts together, and measurements and dimensions check the result.
Parts export to STL and OBJ for the slicer. STL, OBJ and DXF files can be imported, and extensions written in Lua add commands that build parametric geometry such as gears and boxes.

description.p: The second release candidate of Xtrude CAD 0.1.0.

ul.li: Documents are saved in Xtrude CAD's own format, .xtrude. IngeTrazo .igz documents still open, as new unsaved documents, and are no longer written.
3MF export, for slicers that read it.
Menus and toolbars organised around the work on a part, with stacked toolbar buttons for related tools.
One Import… and one Export… command; the file dialog lists the formats. Opening a file that is not a document starts a new document holding it.
Push/pull refuses a push that would break the solid while dragging, and keeps the solid on fine curves.
Copies of an imported .skp component keep one shared definition.
The unfinished image export is removed.

description.p: The first release of Xtrude CAD.

ul.li: Push/pull modelling with lengths typed as you draw, in millimetres by default.
Lines, rectangles, circles and arcs; offset, fillet, sweep, move, rotate and scale; groups and components; measurements and dimensions.
STL and OBJ export for the slicer; STEP, STL, OBJ and DXF import.
Opens and saves .igz documents, compatible with IngeTrazo.
Lua extensions, with gear and box examples.
A portable tarball for x86_64 Linux and a Flatpak bundle.
